content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

## Example 1 (2025-05-19)
- Model forecasts are generally lower than true outcomes after day 5
- Looking at the divergence:
  - Days 1-5: Model is slightly below reality (minor error)
  - Days 6-10: Model 70.69 vs True 72.61 (underestimated by ~2.9)
  - Days 11-15: Model 71.41 vs True 73.50 (underestimated by ~2.1)
  - Days 16-20: Model 72.29 vs True 74.23 (underestimated by ~1.9)
  - Days 21-25: Model 71.08 vs True 72.66 (underestimated by ~1.6)
  - Days 26-30: Model 69.23 vs True 70.96 (underestimated by ~1.7)

The model is consistently UNDERFORECASTING by about 2-3 points throughout.

Looking at sentiment vs error:
- When sentiment is positive (0.67, 1.00), model underforecasts more
- When sentiment is negative, errors are smaller

## Example 2 (2025-05-16)
Very similar to Example 1, with nearly identical forecast and outcome arrays. The model underforecasts by about 2-3 points as well.

## Example 3 (2024-08-14)
Let me look at this more carefully:
- Model forecasts start around 71.88 and gradually decline to 73.19
- True outcomes: start around 71.87 but then TAILLY UP significantly

Looking at the divergence:
- Days 1-5: Model ~72.7 vs True ~72.8-73.7 (minor)
- Days 6-10: Model ~72.7 vs True ~70.5-71.5 (model overforecasted by ~2 points)


- Days 11-15: Model ~71.9 vs True ~66.2-70.4 (model overforecasted by ~4-6 points!)
- Days 16-20: Model ~71.6 vs True ~62.8-66.5 (model overforecasted by ~5-9 points!)
- Days 21-25: Model ~70.6 vs True ~61.3-64.3
